settings.sentence: The text Claude Code adds to commit messages and pull request descriptions, or none at all.
settings.summary: The text Claude Code adds to your commits and pull requests, or none.
settings.eli5: When Claude makes a commit or a pull request, it adds a short note that Claude helped. This setting changes that note or hides it.
settings.impact: Reviewers see the custom text, or no note at all. The value false needs Claude Code v2.1.281 or later; older versions skip the whole settings file that holds it.

suggest.reason: Offer built-in text, custom text or hidden (false, needs v2.1.281 or later). A project rule that already states the trailer needs no second copy.

settings.default: unset (auto in terminal and VS Code sessions since v2.1.283)
settings.sentence: The permission mode new sessions start in; manual is the name of default (it asks before most actions).
settings.summary: The permission mode a new session starts in.
settings.eli5: It decides how often Claude stops to ask you before it acts. Some modes ask for almost everything, others for almost nothing.
settings.impact: A mode that asks less is faster but lets more actions run without your check. auto and bypassPermissions take effect from your user file only, not from a project or local file. Unset, the built-in start mode of your surface applies.

suggest.reason: Leave unset: auto is the built-in start mode since v2.1.283, and auto or bypassPermissions in a project or local file is silently ignored.

settings.sentence: The model Claude Code starts with, an alias or a full model ID.
settings.summary: The model new Claude Code sessions start with.
settings.eli5: Claude comes as several models, some faster and cheaper, some stronger. This picks the one every new session starts with, and you can still switch during a session.
settings.impact: Speed, cost and quality follow the model you pick (unverified: the reference page names no prices). An organization default model set by an admin wins over this key. --model and ANTHROPIC_MODEL override it for one session.

suggest.reason: Leave unset.

settings.sentence: The default effort for models without a saved level of their own; in the user file Opus 5.5 and later ignore it, and Haiku 5.5 (default medium) most likely does too, since it came after Opus 5.5 (inferred from the docs wording).
settings.summary: The default effort level for models without a saved level of their own.
settings.eli5: Effort is how hard Claude thinks before it answers. Low is quick and cheap, high thinks longer.
settings.impact: Lower levels are faster and cheaper on simple tasks; higher levels reason more deeply and spend more tokens. In the user file Opus 5.5 and later models ignore it and start at their own default until /effort saves a level for them under modelSettings. --effort and CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL override it for one session.

suggest.reason: Leave unset; if effort is wanted, write modelSettings.<model>.effortLevel (what /effort writes) in Advanced. The global setup offers the level of claude-haiku-5-5 as an optional change, off by default.

settings.sentence: The model that answers when Claude calls the advisor tool; it must rank at least as high as the main model.
settings.summary: The model that answers when Claude calls the advisor tool; unset turns the advisor off.
settings.eli5: Claude can ask a second model for advice on hard steps. This picks that second model, which must be at least as capable as the main one.
settings.impact: The advisor may use more tokens, so sessions can cost more. It has no effect where the advisor is not available, such as Amazon Bedrock. CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ADVISOR_TOOL turns the advisor off, and this key cannot turn it back on.

suggest.reason: Off by default: experimental, extra token cost, Anthropic API only.

settings.sentence: Connect Remote Control automatically when an interactive session starts.
settings.summary: Connect Remote Control automatically when an interactive session starts.
settings.eli5: Remote Control lets you continue a session on this machine from your phone, a tablet or a browser. With this on, every session connects without you asking.
settings.impact: Every session can then be reached from claude.ai/code and the Claude app. A true in a project or local file is ignored, so a repository can turn it off but not on. --remote-control turns it on for one session.

suggest.reason: Opt-in: while connected, the session transcript is stored on Anthropic servers.

settings.sentence: Opts out of error reporting; any value counts as set, including 0 and false.
settings.summary: Opts out of error reporting.
settings.eli5: When Claude Code hits an error, it can send an error report. This stops those reports.
settings.impact: No error reports leave the machine. Any value counts as set, even 0 or false; remove the variable to turn reporting back on.

settings.sentence: Turns off the "How is Claude doing?" session quality surveys.
settings.summary: Turns off the "How is Claude doing?" session quality surveys.
settings.eli5: Now and then Claude Code asks you to rate the session. This stops those questions.
settings.impact: No more rating prompts in your sessions. The feedbackSurveyRate setting lowers how often they appear instead of turning them off.

settings.sentence: Disables the /feedback command, Claude-drafted feedback, /bug and /share.
settings.summary: Turns off /feedback, Claude-drafted feedback, /bug and /share.
settings.eli5: Claude Code has commands to send feedback or share a session. This turns them off.
settings.impact: You can no longer send feedback or share a session from Claude Code. The older name DISABLE_BUG_COMMAND is also accepted.

settings.sentence: Opts out of telemetry and stops feature-flag fetching; any value counts as set, including 0 and false.
settings.summary: Opts out of telemetry and stops feature-flag fetching.
settings.eli5: Claude Code sends usage events and asks Anthropic which features to switch on. This stops both.
settings.impact: Features that need flag fetching stop working, such as /import and /skill-doctor; for Remote Control the docs point to its own requirements. Session quality surveys stop too. Any value counts as set, even 0 or false.

suggest.reason: Never preset: it turns flag fetching off, so the advisor stays off and idle compaction and /import go.

settings.sentence: Opts out of telemetry like DISABLE_TELEMETRY, including the stop of flag fetching; 0 leaves telemetry on.
settings.summary: Opts out of telemetry like DISABLE_TELEMETRY, flag fetching included.
settings.eli5: Many developer tools read this one switch to stop sending usage data. Claude Code reads it too.
settings.impact: The same effect as DISABLE_TELEMETRY: features that need flag fetching, such as /import, stop working. 0 leaves telemetry on.

suggest.reason: Never preset: it turns flag fetching off.

settings.sentence: Stops feature-flag fetching and uses code defaults for every flag; 0 leaves fetching on.
settings.summary: Stops feature-flag fetching; every flag uses its code default.
settings.eli5: Claude Code asks Anthropic which features to switch on. This stops asking and uses the built-in defaults.
settings.impact: Remote Control and the other features that need flag fetching become unavailable. Telemetry stays on unless DISABLE_TELEMETRY is set too. 0 or false leaves fetching on.

suggest.reason: Never preset: Remote Control and the advisor become unavailable.

settings.sentence: Stops auto-updates, telemetry, error reporting, feedback and flag fetching; any value counts as set, including 0 and false.
settings.summary: Stops nonessential traffic: auto-updates, telemetry, error reports, feedback and flag fetching.
settings.eli5: Besides your actual work, Claude Code goes online for extras like updates and usage data. This turns all those extras off at once.
settings.impact: Auto-updates stop, so you update by hand. Remote Control and the other features that need flag fetching become unavailable. Any value counts as set, even 0 or false.

suggest.reason: Never preset: it also stops auto-updates and makes Remote Control unavailable.

settings.sentence: How Claude Code notifies you when a task completes or a permission prompt waits.
settings.summary: How Claude Code tells you a task finished or a prompt waits.
settings.eli5: When Claude is done or needs you, it can ring the terminal bell or show a desktop notice. This picks which.
settings.impact: With auto, iTerm2, Ghostty and Kitty get desktop notifications and most other terminals get nothing. terminal_bell rings in any terminal. notifications_disabled sends none.

suggest.reason: Docs default.

settings.sentence: The interface color theme, built-in or a custom one.
settings.summary: The interface color theme, built-in or custom.
settings.eli5: It sets the colors Claude Code uses in your terminal. There are light, dark and colorblind-friendly choices.
settings.impact: auto follows your terminal's light or dark background. The daltonized themes use colorblind-friendly colors; the ansi themes use only your terminal's palette.

settings.sentence: Changes Claude's role, tone and output format with a built-in or custom output style.
settings.summary: An output style that changes Claude's role, tone and output format.
settings.eli5: An output style is a saved set of instructions for how Claude talks to you. Explanatory, for example, adds short explanations while it works.
settings.impact: Claude's answers change in role, tone and format. A change during a session applies from your next message and keeps the prompt cache.

settings.sentence: A command that renders the status line below the prompt; edit it in the file, the app shows it.
settings.summary: A command that draws a status line below the prompt.
settings.eli5: You can show a line under the prompt with the model, the cost or the git branch. This names the command that prints it.
settings.impact: It runs your own command, so that command must be installed here. With allowManagedHooksOnly on, or disableAllHooks set outside managed settings, only the managed value runs.

settings.sentence: Runs Bash commands in a sandbox on macOS, Linux and WSL2.
settings.summary: Runs Bash commands in a sandbox on macOS, Linux and WSL2.
settings.eli5: A sandbox is a closed box for commands: they reach only the files and sites that are allowed. This puts Claude's shell commands in that box.
settings.impact: Commands get limited file and network access, which limits what a bad command can do. Linux and WSL2 need bubblewrap and socat. When the sandbox cannot start, commands run without it unless failIfUnavailable is true.

suggest.reason: On where the platform supports it, per project (project setup writes it to the local file). Linux and WSL2 need bubblewrap and socat; without them commands run unsandboxed unless failIfUnavailable is true.

settings.default: unset (false: commands run unsandboxed when the sandbox cannot start)
settings.sentence: Stops Claude Code at startup when the sandbox cannot start, instead of running commands without it.
settings.summary: Refuse to start when the sandbox cannot, instead of running unsandboxed.
settings.eli5: If the sandbox cannot start, Claude Code normally keeps going without it. With this on, it stops instead.
settings.impact: When the sandbox cannot start, Claude Code exits at startup instead of running commands unsandboxed, so it does not start on a platform the sandbox does not support. It applies only when sandbox.enabled is true.

suggest.reason: With sandbox.enabled on, a missing bubblewrap or socat otherwise leaves every command unsandboxed without a stop. Setup does not write it: it is the user's choice, via benchkeeper settings set.

settings.default: unset (true: a blocked command may be retried outside the sandbox)
settings.sentence: Lets Claude retry a command the sandbox blocked outside the sandbox; false forbids the retry.
settings.summary: Lets Claude retry a blocked command outside the sandbox.
settings.eli5: When the sandbox blocks a command, Claude can ask to run it outside the box. false takes that option away.
settings.impact: false is stricter: while the sandbox runs, commands stay sandboxed unless excludedCommands names them. A task that needs more than the sandbox allows then fails (unverified). Your permission mode and allow rules decide who approves a retry.

suggest.reason: A prompt injection can ask for the unsandboxed retry. False closes it; a tool that needs full access goes in sandbox.excludedCommands. Setup does not write it.

settings.sentence: Strips credentials from the environments of the Bash commands, hooks and stdio MCP servers Claude Code starts; GitHub tokens and proxy settings stay.
settings.summary: Strips credentials from the environment of the commands, hooks and MCP servers Claude starts.
settings.eli5: Programs Claude starts normally see the secret tokens in your environment. This hides them from those programs, except GitHub tokens and proxy settings.
settings.impact: A prompt injection can read fewer secrets; Claude Code keeps them for its own API calls. A tool that needs a credential from the environment may stop working (unverified). It also turns sandbox auto-allow off.

suggest.reason: A prompt injection that runs a command can read provider and cloud tokens from the environment. Leave it unset if a subprocess needs one of the removed variables.

settings.sentence: Rules that stop Claude's file tools from reading a path. Doctor expects Read rules for the .ssh, .aws and .config/gh folders (the last holds the GitHub CLI login), for example Read(//**/.ssh/**); a script that opens the files itself is not covered.
settings.summary: Rules for tool uses Claude Code blocks, such as reading a secrets folder.
settings.eli5: A deny rule names things Claude must never do, like opening your SSH keys. Claude's tools refuse them.
settings.impact: Matching files drop out of search, and Claude cannot read or edit them. A command that reads files without naming them, such as grep -r, is not covered; the sandbox covers that. Doctor expects Read rules for the .ssh, .aws and .config/gh folders.

settings.sentence: Days Claude Code keeps session transcripts before a silent sweep deletes them; the Sessions board reads them.
settings.summary: Days Claude Code keeps session transcripts before deleting them.
settings.eli5: Claude Code keeps a record of your past sessions. After this many days it deletes old ones without a message.
settings.impact: Deleted sessions leave /resume and the Sessions board. 0 fails validation, so use a large number for long retention.

suggest.reason: Keep the default 30 or higher: transcripts are deleted without a message (anthropics/claude-code#59248), and a lower value shortens the Sessions board history.

settings.sentence: The release channel auto-updates follow; stable is about one week old and skips major regressions.
settings.summary: The release channel auto-updates follow: latest or stable.
settings.eli5: Updates can arrive as soon as they are out, or about a week later once they settled. stable waits.
settings.impact: stable skips releases with major regressions and gets new features about a week later. Homebrew installs ignore this key. In managed settings it enforces one channel for everyone.

suggest.reason: About one week old and skips major regressions, the same idea as the app's 7-day rule for tools.

settings.sentence: How long the main conversation's prompt cache holds: 5 minutes, or an hour at a higher cache write cost.
settings.summary: How long the prompt cache holds the main conversation: 5 minutes or 1 hour.
settings.eli5: Claude Code keeps the conversation in a cache between requests. This sets how long the cache lasts while you pause.
settings.impact: 1h keeps the cache warm across longer breaks, but each cache write is billed at a higher rate. It needs Claude Code v2.1.242 or later. FORCE_PROMPT_CACHING_5M and CLAUDE_CODE_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL override it.

settings.sentence: Includes the built-in commit and pull request instructions and the git status snapshot in Claude's context.
settings.summary: Includes the built-in commit and pull request instructions and the git status snapshot.
settings.eli5: Claude gets built-in tips on writing commits and a snapshot of your git state. false leaves both out.
settings.impact: With false, Claude starts without your branch and git status and follows only your own git instructions. CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_GIT_INSTRUCTIONS overrides it for one session.

settings.sentence: Lets Claude read from and write to the auto memory directory.
settings.summary: Lets Claude read from and write to the auto memory directory.
settings.eli5: Claude can save notes in a memory folder and read them again in later sessions. false turns that off.
settings.impact: With false, Claude neither reads nor writes its auto memory. CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY overrides it for one session, in either direction.

suggest.reason: Off, the memory index (its first 200 lines or 25 KB) no longer loads at session start; the /memory toggle switches it back, but a false in a project or local settings file overrides it and must be changed there.

settings.sentence: Skips the WebFetch hostname check when Anthropic is unreachable.
settings.summary: Skips the WebFetch hostname check that asks Anthropic first.
settings.eli5: Before Claude fetches a web page, Claude Code sends the site's name to Anthropic for a safety check. This skips that check.
settings.impact: It helps where traffic to Anthropic is blocked, such as some Amazon Bedrock setups. WebFetch then tries any URL without the blocklist, so add WebFetch permission rules to limit the domains.

settings.sentence: Deprecated: use attribution; false drops the commit trailer and the pull request text unless attribution sets them.
settings.summary: Deprecated: use attribution.
settings.eli5: An older switch for the note that Claude helped with a commit. The attribution setting replaces it.
settings.impact: false drops the commit trailer and the pull request text. Claude Code ignores it once attribution sets commit or pr.

settings.sentence: Rules that always prompt, also in auto mode, where a pull request or a push to the default branch would otherwise pass the classifier. Bash(git push *) and Bash(gh pr create *) are the two checkpoints; a push through git -C dir push does not match, so use a PreToolUse hook for a hard stop.
settings.summary: Rules for tool uses that always prompt you, even in modes that would allow them.
settings.eli5: An ask rule makes Claude stop and ask you before a certain action, like a git push. It asks even when it would normally go ahead.
settings.impact: More prompts, and a check before risky steps such as a push or a pull request. In dontAsk mode a matching use is denied instead. A push written as git -C dir push does not match Bash(git push *) (unverified).

suggest.reason: A human checkpoint on push and pull request creation, for people who run several repositories. Setup writes none; it costs one prompt per push.

settings.sentence: Makes the file tools refuse reads outside the working directories in every permission mode, and with the sandbox on denies sandboxed commands reads of the home folder. Sibling repositories then need /add-dir or permissions.additionalDirectories.
settings.summary: Makes the file tools refuse reads outside the working directories.
settings.eli5: Claude can then read files only in the folders you work in. To read another folder, you add it with /add-dir.
settings.impact: Files elsewhere on the machine stay out of reach of the file tools, but work across sibling repositories needs /add-dir. Shell commands the parser cannot trace prompt even in auto mode. A true in any file applies, so a repository can turn the block on but cannot lift yours.

suggest.reason: One key instead of a growing deny list; plan for the folders a session must still read.

settings.sentence: Disclosure: with the sandbox on, sandboxed commands run without a permission prompt by default; false prompts for them. A repository's own settings file can set it; only managed settings stop that.
settings.summary: Runs sandboxed Bash commands without a permission prompt.
settings.eli5: When a command runs inside the sandbox, Claude Code trusts the box and does not ask you. false makes it ask as usual.
settings.impact: On by default, so sandboxed commands run unasked; deny rules and specific ask rules such as Bash(git push *) still apply. false brings back the regular prompts. CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB turns auto-allow off.

suggest.reason: Leave unset to keep the default (true); set false to prompt for sandboxed commands.

settings.sentence: User settings only: project and local files are not read for it. Rules for the auto mode classifier; a list replaces the built-in section unless it holds "$defaults". Writing the key replaces the whole object, soft_deny, environment, hard_deny and classifyAllShell included.
settings.summary: Your own rules for the auto mode classifier, from the user or managed file only.
settings.eli5: In auto mode a checker decides which actions are safe without asking you. Here you tell it what your organization trusts or forbids.
settings.impact: A list without "$defaults" replaces the built-in rules of that list. Project and local files are not read for this key. Writing the key here replaces the whole object.

allow: Allow `gh pr merge` in the session's repository when the user's message asks to merge that pull request; never with --admin or --force, never for CI changes, and never for a merge the agent starts itself.

suggest.reason: Auto mode blocks a merge nobody approved, and a squash merge is the same command. Whether the classifier honours the exclusion clauses is unverified.

bundles.label: Less noise
bundles.sentence: Error reporting, the quality survey and the feedback command off; none of them turns off flag fetching, so the advisor keeps working.

settings.sentence: The model Codex uses.
settings.summary: The model Codex uses.
settings.eli5: Codex can run on several models. This picks which one.
settings.impact: Speed, cost and quality follow the model (unverified: the reference names no prices). Pick a model your signed-in account or workspace can use.

settings.sentence: Reasoning effort, a value the selected model advertises, such as low, medium or high.
settings.summary: Reasoning effort, one of the levels the selected model advertises.
settings.eli5: Effort is how long Codex thinks before it answers. Higher levels think longer.
settings.impact: Higher effort spends more tokens and time (unverified). The available levels depend on the model and the client.

settings.sentence: When Codex pauses for approval before running commands; a granular table form exists and is shown, not edited.
settings.summary: When Codex pauses for your approval before running commands.
settings.eli5: It decides when Codex stops to ask you before it runs a command.
settings.impact: Fewer pauses are faster but let more run without your check (unverified). untrusted is no longer supported. The granular table form is shown, not edited.

suggest.reason: Codex recommends on-request with workspace-write in version-controlled folders; it may start read-only until a directory is trusted. Never offered: never together with danger-full-access.

settings.sentence: Sandbox policy for file and network access while commands run.
settings.summary: Sandbox policy for file and network access while commands run.
settings.eli5: It sets how much a command Codex runs may touch: read only, write in the workspace, or everything.
settings.impact: danger-full-access lifts the limits, so a bad command can reach the whole machine (unverified). read-only and workspace-write keep commands inside their bounds.

suggest.reason: Pairs with on-request (see approval_policy); or leave both unset.

settings.sentence: Web search mode: cached results by default, live only on request.
settings.summary: Web search mode: cached by default, or indexed, live or disabled.
settings.eli5: Codex can search the web. cached uses a search index without going to the open web, live fetches real pages.
settings.impact: live gets current pages but reaches the open web; disabled removes the tool. With --yolo or another full access sandbox setting the default is live.

suggest.reason: Leave unset (cached); live only on request.

settings.sentence: false turns off OpenAI analytics on this machine and the custom OTLP metrics exporters.
settings.summary: Turns analytics on or off for this machine or profile.
settings.eli5: Codex can send usage statistics. false stops them.
settings.impact: In Codex CLI, false also turns off custom OTLP metrics exporters. Unset, the client default applies.

suggest.reason: The less-noise switch: documented key; also stops custom OTLP metrics exporters.

settings.sentence: false turns off feedback collection across Codex surfaces.
settings.summary: Feedback through /feedback across local clients.
settings.eli5: Codex lets you send feedback with /feedback. false turns that off.
settings.impact: With false you cannot send feedback from Codex. It is on by default.

suggest.reason: The less-noise switch.

settings.sentence: A command Codex runs for notifications; it receives a JSON payload.
settings.summary: A command Codex runs for notifications.
settings.eli5: When Codex has news for you, it can run a program of yours. That program gets the details as JSON.
settings.impact: The command must exist on this machine. Codex ignores this key in a project's .codex/config.toml, so put it in the user file.

settings.sentence: Desktop notifications from the terminal UI (a list of event types is shown, not edited).
settings.summary: Desktop notifications from the terminal UI.
settings.eli5: The Codex terminal app can show a notice when something happens. A list limits it to some events.
settings.impact: Off, you check the terminal yourself. A list of event types is shown here, not edited.

settings.sentence: Whether Codex saves session history to history.jsonl.
settings.summary: Whether Codex saves session transcripts to history.jsonl.
settings.eli5: Codex can keep a file of your past sessions. none keeps nothing in it.
settings.impact: none leaves no transcripts in history.jsonl; save-all keeps them on disk. What else reads that file is not named (unverified).

settings.sentence: Checks for Codex updates on startup; set false only when updates are managed centrally.
settings.summary: Checks for Codex updates on startup.
settings.eli5: Each time Codex starts, it looks for a newer version. false stops that check.
settings.impact: With false you may miss updates and fixes. Set false only when updates are managed centrally.
